{"id": "af8dfaf7d74d4a6f8e9255076b144a6d", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Fast agent report: a separate fast agent investigated this same incident in parallel and has finished. This is its whole final report, shared once. Nobody has checked it.

## Root cause
The limit is at the EBS volume layer: io2 vol-0123456789abcdef0 (10 GiB) is set to 1,000 IOPS. In every 5-minute period from 18:30 to 19:30 UTC, it handled exactly 1,000 IOPS. The work is all writes, a constant 8 KiB each, about 7.8 MiB/s. A flat line at exactly the provisioned number means the volume is at its limit, so extra requests wait in the queue. VolumeQueueLength stayed around 1.27–1.50, and at this I/O rate that matches the measured ~1.3–1.5 ms per-write latency. That queue is what tripped the alarm example-a-io2-queue-length (threshold 1.0), which went to ALARM at 18:11:04 UTC. The instance is not the bottleneck. i-1234567890abcdef0_5 is a c6i.xlarge rated for 6,000 baseline / 40,000 burst IOPS and 156.25 / 1,250 MB/s. Its InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck and InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck were 0 throughout, and EBSIOBalance% and EBSByteBalance% stayed at 99%. Throughput is not a limit either: 7.8 MiB/s is far below both the volume and instance ceilings. Recommended fix: raise this volume's provisioned IOPS with ModifyVolume (online, no detach). io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB, so 10 GiB permits up to 10,000 IOPS. Size it to the real peak write rate with headroom, e.g. 3,000–5,000 IOPS. Stay at or under 6,000 total IOPS across this instance's EBS volumes so you don't swap the volume limit for the instance's baseline limit. If you need more than 6,000 sustained, move to a larger instance size. Changing the volume type or increasing size alone won't help unless IOPS goes up. A cost-saving alternative is to batch or coalesce the application's 8 KiB writes into larger I/Os.
## Evidence
- EC2 DescribeVolumes: vol-0123456789abcdef0 is io2, 10 GiB, Iops=1000, attached at /dev/sdf to i-1234567890abcdef0_5.
- CloudWatch AWS/EBS (VolumeReadOps+VolumeWriteOps)/period: exactly 1000.0 IOPS in every 5-minute period from 18:30 to 19:25 UTC (19:15 showed 907; the 19:30 period is incomplete). The rate is flat at the provisioned limit.
- CloudWatch AWS/EBS VolumeWriteBytes/VolumeWriteOps: a constant 8 KiB per write, 7.81 MiB/s. The workload is small writes, so IOPS is the limit, not throughput.
- CloudWatch AWS/EBS VolumeQueueLength avg: 1.47–1.50 from 18:30 to 19:10, 1.27–1.33 from 19:15 to 19:30. VolumeTotalWriteTime/ops gives ~1.27–1.50 ms per write, which matches the queueing.
- CloudWatch alarm example-a-io2-queue-length: ALARM since 2026-11-23 18:11:04 UTC (VolumeQueueLength 1.49–1.50 \u003e 1.0 for 3 of 3 datapoints).
- CloudWatch AWS/EC2 i-1234567890abcdef0_5: InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck=0 and InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck=0 for every period from 18:30 to 19:30. EBSIOBalance% and EBSByteBalance% were 99% the whole time, so the instance-level EBS limit is not binding.
- EC2 DescribeInstanceTypes c6i.xlarge: BaselineIops 6000 (max 40000), BaselineThroughput 156.25 MB/s (max 1250), far above the ~1,000 IOPS / 7.8 MiB/s being used.
## Affected resources
- vol-0123456789abcdef0
- i-1234567890abcdef0_5
- example-a-io2-queue-length
## Gaps
- VolumeIOPSExceededCheck and VolumeThroughputExceededCheck returned no datapoints for this volume, so the saturation call rests on observed IOPS sitting flat at the provisioned value, not on a direct exceeded flag.
- I didn't measure how much IOPS the application actually wants beyond 1,000, so the recommended new IOPS number is an estimate. Check it against the application's write rate or the OS-level iostat queue depth.
- I didn't check the I/O load on the other volumes attached to the instance (vol-1234567890abcdef0_20, vol-1234567890abcdef0_19, vol-1234567890abcdef0_16). They share the instance's 6,000 baseline IOPS, which matters when choosing the new provisioned IOPS.
- I didn't capture a baseline period from before the alarm (it started around 18:08). The volume was already at its limit across all the data examined.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

**Volume layer (binding):**
- **Writes are pinned at the limit.** Every 1-minute period from 18:10 to 19:33 UTC shows 1,000.0 writes/s. VolumeConsumedReadWriteOps is 60,000 per minute, which equals the 1,000 IOPS provisioned.
- **The workload is small writes.** It is all writes, a constant 8 KiB each, about 7.8 MiB/s. That is IOPS-bound, nowhere near the volume's throughput ceiling.
- **The queue and latency match a capped volume.** VolumeQueueLength was 1.47–1.51 from 18:10 to 19:15, then about 1.27 afterwards. Write time per write was about 1.49 ms, then about 1.27 ms. Both are what 1,000 IOPS at that queue depth works out to: requests wait at the cap. The alarm (`example-a-io2-queue-length`, threshold 1.0) went to ALARM at 18:11:04.

**Instance layer (not binding yet, but close on throughput):**
- **Nothing flags it as limited now.** The c6i.xlarge's "limit exceeded" checks (InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck and InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck) are 0. Its EBS IO and byte balances (EBSIOBalance%, EBSByteBalance%) stay at 99%, and CPU is about 1%.
- **IOPS has room.** The instance does about 1,501 IOPS against a 6,000 baseline.
- **Throughput does not have much room.** Another volume on the same instance, gp3 vol-1234567890abcdef0_19, is reading a steady 125 MiB/s (its own cap). That puts total instance EBS throughput at about 132.9 MiB/s. The instance's baseline is 156.25 MB/s (about 149 MiB/s), so it is already at about 89%.

**What to change:**
1. **Raise IOPS on the io2 volume.** Use `ModifyVolume`, which works online with no detach. 10 GiB of io2 allows up to 10,000 IOPS. Each extra 1,000 IOPS at 8 KiB adds about 7.8 MiB/s.
2. **Stop around 3,000 IOPS unless you also free throughput.** Up to about 3,000 IOPS stays under the instance's throughput baseline while the gp3 read stream keeps running. Beyond that, you would swap the volume limit for the instance's: the byte balance starts draining, then throttling begins.
3. **If you need more than ~3,000 IOPS**, either:
   - throttle or move the 125 MiB/s read workload on vol-1234567890abcdef0_19, or
   - move to a larger instance size with a higher EBS throughput baseline.
4. **Optional, cheaper:** have the application batch or combine its 8 KiB writes into larger ones, so it needs fewer IOPS.

- The volume-level "exceeded" check and average-latency metrics exist for this volume but returned no data. So the saturation call rests on the flat 1,000 IOPS line and the consumed-ops count, not a direct flag.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### io2 volume queue length above threshold
**Description:** Alarm example-a-io2-queue-length (AWS/EBS VolumeQueueLength Average > 1.0, 60s x 3, TreatMissingData notBreaching) on vol-0123456789abcdef0 went to ALARM at 2026-11-23 18:11:04 UTC. It fired on 3 datapoints: 1.50 at 18:08, 1.49 at 18:09 and 1.49 at 18:10. The alarm has no actions configured. Queue length then held at about 1.27–1.5. The volume has never been modified.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T18:08:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Write workload saturating provisioned 1000 IOPS
**Description:** A sustained 8 KiB write workload is running at exactly the io2 volume's provisioned 1000 IOPS, so additional I/O queues and VolumeQueueLength rises to about 1.5. Instance-level EBS balances are at 99%, so the volume's own IOPS cap is the likely limit.
**Cascades to:** symptom-io2-queue-length

#### Supporting Observations
- **Write IOPS pinned at provisioned 1000:** Write IOPS on vol-0123456789abcdef0 held at exactly 1,000 (the provisioned io2 value) from 18:10 to 19:35 UTC. The writes are a constant 8 KiB, about 7.8 MiB/s. VolumeConsumedReadWriteOps is 60,000 per minute (1,000/s) every minute from 19:10 to 19:34, except a dip to 32,164 at 19:16. VolumeIOPSExceededCheck, VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeStalledIOCheck returned no datapoints.
- **Instance EBS limits not constrained:** c6i.xlarge i-1234567890abcdef0_5 is rated for 6,000 baseline / 40,000 burst IOPS and 156.25 / 1,250 MB/s. From 18:50 to 19:30, InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck and InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck were 0 in every period. EBSIOBalance% and EBSByteBalance% stayed at 99%. Instance totals are about 1,500 IOPS and about 133 MiB/s.

#### Gaps
- **Volume exceeded-check and avg-latency metrics returned no data:** VolumeIOPSExceededCheck, VolumeThroughputExceededCheck, VolumeAvgWriteLatency, VolumeAvgIOPS and VolumeStalledIOCheck exist for vol-0123456789abcdef0 but returned no datapoints. The saturation conclusion therefore rests on the flat 1,000 IOPS line and the consumed-ops count, not on a direct flag.

### Root Cause: io2 volume under-provisioned at 1,000 IOPS for its write workload
**Description:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (example-a-io2, 10 GiB io2, account 012345678901_1, us-east-1) is set to 1,000 IOPS. Its constant 8 KiB write workload (about 7.8 MiB/s) has saturated that limit since about 18:08 UTC. The volume's own provisioned IOPS is the binding constraint, not the c6i.xlarge instance. Raising provisioned IOPS through ModifyVolume removes it.
**Cascades to:** finding-iops-cap

#### Supporting Observations
- **Write IOPS pinned at provisioned 1000:** Write IOPS on vol-0123456789abcdef0 held at exactly 1,000 (the provisioned io2 value) from 18:10 to 19:35 UTC. The writes are a constant 8 KiB, about 7.8 MiB/s. VolumeConsumedReadWriteOps is 60,000 per minute (1,000/s) every minute from 19:10 to 19:34, except a dip to 32,164 at 19:16. VolumeIOPSExceededCheck, VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeStalledIOCheck returned no datapoints.
- **Instance EBS limits not constrained:** c6i.xlarge i-1234567890abcdef0_5 is rated for 6,000 baseline / 40,000 burst IOPS and 156.25 / 1,250 MB/s. From 18:50 to 19:30, InstanceEBSIOPSExceededCheck and InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck were 0 in every period. EBSIOBalance% and EBSByteBalance% stayed at 99%. Instance totals are about 1,500 IOPS and about 133 MiB/s.

#### Gaps
- **Actual application write demand unknown:** The volume caps visible write IOPS at 1,000, so the rate the application actually wants cannot be seen. Check the OS-level queue (iostat aqu-sz) or the app's write rate before choosing the final IOPS value.
- **No healthy baseline period:** Instance i-1234567890abcdef0_5 was launched at 18:05:10 UTC, and the volume has been at its IOPS cap ever since, so there is no healthy period to compare against.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Raise provisioned IOPS on io2 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0 (example-a-io2) from 1,000 to 3,000 with an online ModifyVolume; size and type unchanged.

## Reasoning
The volume is pinned at its 1,000 IOPS cap with 100% 8 KiB writes, so requests queue (queue length ~1.27–1.5, write latency ~1.3–1.5 ms) and the alarm stays in ALARM. 3,000 IOPS is the most the c6i.xlarge can absorb: it is already at ~89% of its 156.25 MB/s EBS baseline due to the 125 MiB/s gp3 reader on vol-1234567890abcdef0_19; +15.6 MiB/s brings it to ~148.5 MiB/s, just under baseline. True write demand above 1,000 IOPS is unknown, and going beyond 3,000 needs lower gp3 read throughput or a larger instance. Cost: ~3x the volume's IOPS cost. After the change, the volume cannot be modified again (including rollback) for 6 hours. Passed the safe-deployment policy check; nothing has been executed.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Record rollback values Iops=1000, Size=10, VolumeType=io2
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 > vol-0123456789abcdef0-backup.json
```
**Purpose:** Record rollback values Iops=1000, Size=10, VolumeType=io2.
**Advisory:** Make sure the backup is of vol-0123456789abcdef0.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Confirm no modification in progress or cooldown (expect…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
```
**Purpose:** Confirm no modification in progress or cooldown (expect InvalidVolumeModification.NotFound).
**Risks:** If a modification completed less than 6 hours ago, stop: the change will be rejected.

#### 2.2 Record the instance's EBS byte balance before the change (expect ~99%)
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name EBSByteBalance% --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value=i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --statistics Minimum --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-30 min' +%FT%TZ) --end-time $(date -u +%FT%TZ)
```
**Purpose:** Record the instance's EBS byte balance before the change (expect ~99%).
**Risks:** If already falling, use a smaller target such as 2,000 IOPS.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Lift the IOPS cap so writes stop queuing; online, no detach or downtime
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --iops 3000
```
**Purpose:** Lift the IOPS cap so writes stop queuing; online, no detach or downtime.
**Risks:** io2 provisioned-IOPS cost rises ~3x., No further modification (including rollback) for 6 hours., If write demand reaches ~3,000/s, instance EBS throughput nears the c6i.xlarge baseline.
**Advisory:** Run once; do not change size or type. Performance may step up gradually while optimizing.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Track the modification to optimizing/completed with TargetIops=3000
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 --query 'VolumesModifications[0].[ModificationState,TargetIops,Progress]'
```
**Purpose:** Track the modification to optimizing/completed with TargetIops=3000.

#### 4.2 Confirm 3000, 10, io2, in-use
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 --query 'Volumes[0].[Iops,Size,VolumeType,State]'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm 3000, 10, io2, in-use.

#### 4.3 Confirm the volume is no longer pinned at the cap; repeat with…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeQueueLength --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --statistics Average --period 60 --start-time $(date -u -d '-15 min' +%FT%TZ) --end-time $(date -u +%FT%TZ)
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the volume is no longer pinned at the cap; repeat with VolumeWriteOps (Sum) and VolumeTotalWriteTime (Sum).
**Advisory:** If writes settle near 180,000/min (3,000/s), demand is at the new cap and this plan is not enough.

#### 4.4 Confirm instance EBS limits stay non-binding (balance ~99%, check 0)
**Type:** text
Re-run the EBSByteBalance% check and check InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck (AWS/EC2, InstanceId=i-1234567890abcdef0_5, Maximum).
**Purpose:** Confirm instance EBS limits stay non-binding (balance ~99%, check 0).
**Risks:** A steadily falling byte balance means the instance is now the bottleneck and the gp3 reader may slow.

#### 4.5 Confirm the alarm returns to OK after 3 datapoints at or below 1.0
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --region us-east-1 --alarm-names example-a-io2-queue-length --query 'MetricAlarms[0].StateValue'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the alarm returns to OK after 3 datapoints at or below 1.0.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Restore the original IOPS if byte balance drains or other volumes are…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --iops 1000
```

## Mitigation Summary

**Action:** Raise provisioned IOPS on io2 volume `vol-0123456789abcdef0` (example-a-io2) from 1,000 to 3,000 with an online ModifyVolume. Size and type stay the same.

**Reasoning:**
- **The cap is the bottleneck.** In account 012345678901_1, us-east-1, volume `[redacted ARN]` has been running at exactly its 1,000 IOPS limit. The workload is 100% writes of 8 KiB each. Requests queue at that cap: VolumeQueueLength is about 1.27–1.5 and write latency is about 1.3–1.5 ms. That is what keeps the alarm in ALARM and the application's write latency high.
- **Why 3,000:** this is the most IOPS the instance can absorb without exceeding its sustained EBS throughput.
  - Instance `[redacted ARN]` is a c6i.xlarge with a 156.25 MB/s EBS baseline.
  - It is already at about 139.4 MB/s (about 89%), mostly because gp3 `vol-1234567890abcdef0_19` reads a steady 125 MiB/s.
  - At 3,000 IOPS × 8 KiB, the io2 volume adds at most about 15.6 MiB/s more. That brings the instance total to about 148.5 MiB/s, still just under the roughly 149 MiB/s baseline.
  - Anything higher would start draining EBSByteBalance% and move the bottleneck to the instance.
  - io2 allows up to 10,000 IOPS at 10 GiB, so 3,000 is within the volume's limits.
- **What this doesn't cover:**
  - **True demand is unknown.** Nobody knows the application's real write demand above 1,000 IOPS. If writes climb to about 3,000/s and stay there, the volume cap may be reached again.
  - **Going further needs a larger change.** Either lower the throughput of the gp3 reader on `vol-1234567890abcdef0_19`, or move to an instance type with a higher EBS baseline. That is a stop/start change, so it isn't proposed as the immediate fix.
- **Cost:** io2 is billed per provisioned IOPS, so this roughly triples the volume's IOPS cost.
- **Rollback limit:** after this change, EBS won't allow another modification of the same volume for at least 6 hours. Pick the value carefully, because you can't revert or tune again right away.
